about: An example tillr backend policy: which adapter program and model fill each seat (the role a run plays). The loop reads this path when no --policy is given. The model names here are placeholders, so no run can start on this file as shipped: copy it, put in the models your credentials reach, and name your copy with --policy. The adapters read none of this file; the drain reads it at staging and puts the values on the adapter's argv. `default_backend` fills an item that names no seat, `seats` maps each seat to a backend, `escalate` lists the backends a failed build moves through, and `backends` declares each adapter with its model and effort. The claude, agy and muse rows are declared and mapped to no seat, to show the row each adapter takes; agy carries its effort inside the model name and takes no effort key.

seat_purposes.design: Settle design decisions and specify the intended change.
seat_purposes.build: Implement the change described by the item or plan.
seat_purposes.review: Review the candidate against the criteria.
seat_purposes.scout: Search the tree and report findings without writing.
seat_purposes.classify: Decide whether delivery is to the repository, a fork, or both without editing either.
seat_purposes.plan: Read the item and tree and write the piece list.
seat_purposes.edit: Apply a settled edit named in the plan.
seat_purposes.test-run: Run a named check and report its result without fixing it.
seat_purposes.verify: Join the pieces and verify the combined result.
seat_purposes.tricky: Implement a change the ordinary build seat has failed at or that is too intricate for it.
seat_purposes.triage: Investigate one unsettled alert episode read-only and file, link, or escalate it.
